segments.text: You're telling me the Great Wall of China isn't just long. It's impossible.
Exactly. People say it's 13,000 miles, but they don't really process what that means.
That's four times the entire U.S. stretched coast to coast, plus another 1,000 miles,
and it was started in 220 B.C. before Jesus, before most empires even existed. That's the point.
But how does an ancient civilization build something that massive without modern machines?
It took over a thousand years.
No empire commits that kind of time
And here's the part nobody talks about.
The steep defensive side, the battlements,
they're facing China, not the outside.
So the wall wasn't built to keep people out.
It was built to keep something in,
it may not be Chinese at all,
but a leftover structure from the old Tartarian empire.
If that's true, then you have to ask yourself,
what were they trying to contain?
And why is everyone so quiet about it?
